lines.text: Here is the third term in the training bill: activations.
Every layer passes its output to the next one, and the backward pass needs those outputs to work out the gradients.
So you keep them. All of them. For every layer, for every token in the batch.
And activations are the only term that does not scale with the model. They scale with batch size and sequence length.
Double the sequence length and you double the activation memory.
Which means the term you can control without touching the model is the one that scales with your batch size.
There is a trade available. Do not save the activations. Save only the inputs to a few checkpoints.
Then when the backward pass needs a layer you threw away, recompute it from the last checkpoint.
You traded memory for arithmetic. And arithmetic is the thing a data centre actually has.
The cost is real. A checkpointed step does about a third more work than an uncheckpointed one.
A third more compute to fit twice the batch, or twice the context.
Which is why nobody turns it on for its own sake. You turn it on when the run will not fit.
Throw it away. Compute it again. That is the whole trick.
